newsitem.title: USA: Sierra ends merger with Physician.
newsitem.headline: Sierra ends merger with Physician.

text.p: Sierra Health Services Inc said it is terminating its merger agreement with Physician Corp of America.

Sierra had been re-evaluating the proposed merger since February 20, when Physician said it would take significant additional charges in the fourth quarter of 1996 to cover increased liabilities associated with its workers' compensation division.
The charges represented a material adverse event under the conditions of the original agreement.

On November 4, Sierra agreed to merge with Miami-based Physician in a deal valued at about $480 million. Sierra agreed to exchange 0.45 of its shares for each outstanding share of Physicians in a pooling of interests. The deal was slated to close March 31.

On February 20, Physician said it would take a fourth quarter charge of $80 million related to increased liabilities at its workers' compensation unit. The charge was in addition to a similar charge of $130 million from November 1996.

On March 6 Sierra said extensive losses at Physician's workers' compensation unit prompted it to reassess the terms of the merger, which would have created the eighth largest publicly traded managed care company.
Both companies said on March 6 the merger would not proceed under the currently negotiated terms, but could still go ahead under new terms.
"We were hoping to agree on a transaction that was in the best interests of our shareholders," said Sierra Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Anthony Marlon in a statement Tuesday.
"After a thorough evaluation, however, we could not find a satisfactory alternative."
